samples.title: Branch notebook: Proof strip
samples.statement:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
root is the top node of a binary tree. Examples list nodes one level at a time, from left to right. null marks a missing child; [] means no tree. Each node stores its number in val. Its left and right links point to children. The runner builds the nodes for you. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
A binary tree is a set of nodes, each with a value and up to two children: left and right. root is the top node. Visit a node by recording its value, then visit its whole left branch, then its whole right branch. Use this same rule at every node. Skip missing children. The result list is the recorded values. An empty tree gives an empty result list.

Step 2: Return the answer
Return the whole result list in the order you built it. If it is empty, return [].

Write your function
Complete branchNotebookProofStrip(root, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.
